// 01 — THE PRODUCT & THE ROLLOUT

One assistant. Four zones. Zero guesswork.

The clerk scans a standard 1D barcode; Velo does the searching, sorting and remembering. The human always has final say — Velo organizes, recommends and alerts, never acts alone.

ZONE A→B

Assisted receiving & put-away

Scan the pallet, get a suggested bay, scan the rack to confirm. Batch expiry logged in one tap — no paper checklists at the dock.

ZONE D→C

Checkout-to-refill loop

A POS sale drops shelf stock below threshold; the clerk's phone gets one clear task: oldest batch first, exact bay, exact quantity.

ZONE C

Local RAG copilot

Stock, curing times, TEK17 fire rules — answered in under two seconds, fully on-premise. Nothing sent to any cloud.

NETWORK

Store-first, network-next

Cross-store transfers drafted automatically when a bay runs dry — one-click manager approval.

// THE ROLLOUT

One store, then the map

Nobody re-engineers 300 stores on day one. Prove clarity inside a single store, then let the network grow out of it.

MONTHS 1–3

1 · Empower

Denmark & Norway pilots. Barcode receiving, FEFO rotation, refill loop. Waste down 60%, shelves 99% stocked.

MONTHS 4–6

2 · Connect

Regional goods network. Store-to-store transfers when a backroom runs dry — manager approves in one click.

MONTHS 6–12

3 · Deliver

Sweden & fulfilment. Trucks dispatch only after a scanned pick confirmation at the loading dock.

// 02 — SOVEREIGN BY DEFAULT

100% local AI. Nothing leaves the building.

Velo runs open-weight models on-premise — no external API keys to hijack, no proprietary data crossing the public internet, no cloud outage that can stop a shift. Even offline, the barcode workflows keep running.

Zero external callsInference, embeddings and RAG retrieval run inside Company A's own network or a sovereign European VPC.
Human-in-the-loopVelo never alters stock, disposes goods or orders externally without a scan or a tap from the clerk or manager.
Open-weight stackQuantized Llama 3.2 / Qwen 2.5 via Ollama or vLLM, BGE-M3 embeddings, pgvector — auditable end to end.

// 05 — QUESTIONS

Fair questions, straight answers

Why start with the store clerk, not the delivery fleet?

Every downstream system — transfers, fulfilment, delivery — consumes inventory truth created at the shelf and the bay. Fix the source first and the network scales itself; automate later and you automate chaos.

Is local AI actually fast enough?

Quantized 3B–7B models on a single on-premise GPU answer grounded questions in under two seconds via RAG. The workflow loop — scans, thresholds, tasks — is deterministic logic that doesn't touch the LLM, so the store keeps running even if the GPU naps.

What happens to the legacy infrared scanners?

Retired. A ruggedized smartphone with camera scanning (EAN-13 / Code-128 at under 150ms) replaces $1,500–$2,200 terminals plus 20% annual maintenance contracts — a cut of more than 75% in hardware spend.

How do three markets stay different?

One core, local configuration. Denmark starts with paperless receiving, Norway with standardized zone workflows, Sweden connects fulfilment last. Same platform, three rollout clocks.
